activities.main_competence: 1.0.   Demonstrate mastery of some advanced theories and principles of music
activities.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the fundamentals of music theory
activities.learning_activity: Describe the fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade V (Rhythm, scales and key signatures, and melody and harmony)
suggested_methods: ICT- based learning: Guide students to use different software applications to read and write music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade V
Flash Cards: Provide flashcards of simple known melodies with missing notes or accidentals for students to fill -in
Case Study: Guide students to analyse and present known written musical pieces based on what is covered in ABRSM Music Theory Grade V
activities.assessment_criteria: Fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade V are described correctly

activities.main_competence: 1.0.   Demonstrate mastery of some advanced theories and principles of music
activities.specific_competence: 1.2 Demonstrate an understanding of some advanced theories of music
activities.learning_activity: Describe theories related to the origins of different music traditions in East Africa
suggested_methods: Think-ink-pair-share: Task the students to review literary works on theories related to the origin of music traditions in East Africa and make presentations
activities.assessment_criteria: Theories related to origins of music traditions in East Africa are described correctly
suggested_resources: Audio and video clips of various East African traditional ensemble performances

activities.learning_activity: Sing extended local and foreign songs
suggested_methods: Snow-balling: Provide melodies in flash-cards and snow-ball students to sing individually in different voice parts
activities.assessment_criteria: Extended local and foreign songs are sung correctly
suggested_resources: audio and video clips of extended local and foreign songs

activities.specific_competence: 2.2    Play local and foreign musical instruments
activities.learning_activity: (a) Use music notation software to write music for pitched musical instruments
suggested_methods: ICT-based learning: Task the students to use different notation software to write music for pitched musical instruments
activities.assessment_criteria: Music for pitched musical instruments are written correctly using notation software
suggested_resources: Electronic device installed with a notation software

activities.specific_competence: 2.2    Play local and foreign musical instruments
activities.learning_activity: (b) Use local and foreign musical instruments (strings, percussion and wind) to accompany songs in an ensemble
suggested_methods: Student music clubs: Task students to form musical ensembles and perform songs with local and foreign instrumental accompaniment
Projects: Task the students to accompany patriotic songs using relevant local and foreign musical instruments
activities.assessment_criteria: Song are well accompanied  in an ensemble using local and foreign musical instruments

activities.specific_competence: 2.3   Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of professional ethical conduct in the music industry
activities.learning_activity: Discuss the ethics, norms and values governing the music industry in Tanzania (things that are acceptable, and tolerable against the things that are taboo).
suggested_methods: Problem-based learning: Guide students to identify value and ethics related problems and suggest solutions
Debate: Guide students to debate on the current musical moral standards in Tanzania
Self-reflection: Guide students into self-reflection on their own ethical upbringing in relation to the foreign music industry
activities.assessment_criteria: Ethics, norms and values governing the music industry in Tanzania are well discussed
suggested_resources: BASATA and COSOTA guidelines and audio/ video clips of Tanzanian music

activities.main_competence: 3.0    Use ICT in the music industry
activities.specific_competence: 3.1  Use ICT to produce and master music
activities.learning_activity: (a)   Mix different song productions using ICT
suggested_methods: ICT - based Learning:
Task the students to mix various songs using various music software and present for review
activities.assessment_criteria: Different song productions are mixed successfully using ICT

activities.main_competence: 3.0    Use ICT in the music industry
activities.specific_competence: 3.1  Use ICT to produce and master music
activities.learning_activity: (b) Perform the mastering (finishing) of different song productions using ICT
suggested_methods: ICT - based Learning:
Task students to master music projects using various music software and present for review
activities.assessment_criteria: Different song productions are mastered successfully using ICT

activities.specific_competence: 4.1    Design and conduct a project in music
activities.learning_activity: Design and carry out a project in music
suggested_methods: Project: Facilitate several research projects on music for students to review
Group discussion: Have the students engage in discussions on various musical matters
activities.assessment_criteria: A project in music is designed and carried out successfully
suggested_resources: Videos related to successful music business ventures
and industry reports and market research

activities.main_competence: 1.0. Demonstrate mastery of some advanced theories and principles of music
activities.specific_competence: 1.1   Demonstrate an understanding of the fundamentals of music theory
activities.learning_activity: Describe the fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade VI (Rhythm, and melody and harmony)
suggested_methods: Flash Cards: Handle out flashcards of questions and problems concerning reading and writing music based on what is covered in ABRSM Music Theory Grade VI
Case Study: Guide students to explore known written music based on what is covered in ABRSM Music Theory Grade VI
Problem-based learning: Provide students with erroneous musical pieces for them to detect the errors and write a review.
activities.assessment_criteria: Fundamentals of reading and writing music based on ABRSM Music Theory Grade VI are explained correctly

activities.main_competence: 1.0. Demonstrate mastery of some advanced theories and principles of music
activities.specific_competence: 1.2.  Demonstrate an understanding of some advanced theories of music
activities.learning_activity: Describe the theories related to origins of different music traditions in Africa
suggested_methods: Think-ink-pair-share: Task students to review literary works related to theories on the origins of different music traditions in Africa and make presentations in class
activities.assessment_criteria: Theories related to origins of different music traditions in Africa are explained correctly

suggested_methods: Flash Cards: Handle out flashcards of pieces that need to be transposed

activities.learning_activity: (b) Modulate songs composed in various languages
suggested_methods: ICT-based learning: Task the students to use different music applications to modulate songs composed in various languages
activities.assessment_criteria: Songs composed in various languages are modulated correctly

suggested_methods: ICT-based learning: Task the students to use different music applications to transcribe various song compositions
activities.assessment_criteria: Various song compositions are transcribed correctly

activities.learning_activity: Sing various multi-part songs using relevant techniques
suggested_methods: Snow-balling: Snow-ball different students to sing voice parts individually
Case study: Avail the students with several cases portraying different singing techniques
Student music club: Task students to form music ensembles and sing multi-part songs using relevant techniques
activities.assessment_criteria: Multi-part songs using relevant techniques are sung correctly

activities.specific_competence: 2.3    Play local and foreign musical instruments
activities.learning_activity: (a) Use notation software to write music for  unpitched musical instruments
suggested_methods: ICT-based learning: Task students to use notation software to write music for  unpitched musical instruments
activities.assessment_criteria: Music for unpitched musical instruments are written correctly using notation software
suggested_resources: Electronic device installed with a notation software

activities.specific_competence: 2.3    Play local and foreign musical instruments
activities.learning_activity: (b) Use local and foreign musical instruments (strings, percussion and wind) to accompany contemporary songs in an ensemble
suggested_methods: Student music clubs: In groups, task students to use local and foreign musical instruments to accompany contemporary songs
Projects: Task students with a project to accompany various songs with local and foreign musical instruments in an ensemble performance
activities.assessment_criteria: Local and foreign musical instruments are used correctly to accompany contemporary songs in an ensemble
